question: For one explicitly declared weighted-space quantization of the undensitized V=0 constraint C, is the minimal operator essentially self-adjoint, and if not what endpoint and measurable extension data are required before any C-to-H quantum-equivalence comparison is meaningful?

repository_sources.used_for: the frozen classical C, positive f, H=fC, flat H-hat ordering, and explicit warning that rescaling need not preserve a quantum theory

upstream_results.role: fixes the selected densitized H comparison target but supplies no raw-C operator or equivalence
fixes the selected-H full-p regular-shell completion; it neither authorizes nor answers the independent raw-C audit

primary_sources.source: Louko and Martinez-Pascual, Constraint rescaling in refined algebraic quantisation: momentum constraint, arXiv:1107.1092v2
primary_sources.used_for: explicit branch cases in which classically equivalent rescalings are quantum-equivalent, lack a self-adjoint extension, or acquire extension and superselection ambiguity
primary_sources.not_used_for: proving the endpoint classification or selecting an extension for this V0 differential expression

primary_sources.not_used_for: choosing the raw-C measure, ordering, Fourier decomposition, extension, or physical product

declared_candidate.weighted_auxiliary_space: H_C=L2(R_Q times R_phi, f(Q) dQ dphi)
declared_candidate.fourier_base: Lebesgue p in R, with -i*hbar*d_phi mapped to p
declared_candidate.extension_scope: fixed-p self-adjoint extensions plus a conditional recipe for decomposable extensions that preserve p; no measurable global domain or resolvent field is claimed
declared_candidate.no_selected_extension: theta(p), any parity restriction, and any p-fiber mixing are not supplied by the classical rescaling

assumptions: hbar is strictly positive; numerical diagnostics set hbar=1
the weighted measure, left-weighted ordering, C_c^infinity core, and full Lebesgue-p Fourier base are declared quantization inputs rather than consequences of classical C
the sign-reversed fiber expression is put in the standard real Sturm-Liouville form with leading coefficient 2*hbar^2, weight f>0, and locally integrable potential
Weyl endpoint type is independent of the nonreal spectral parameter once the declared Sturm-Liouville hypotheses hold
the zero-energy modified-Bessel solutions may therefore be used to classify endpoint type, but they do not themselves construct the nonreal deficiency vectors
a fiberwise U(1) extension statement is not promoted to the classification of all full-operator extensions
a Borel theta(p) is necessary but not by itself sufficient for a p-preserving decomposable extension; a measurable field of boundary maps, domains or resolvents must also be supplied
the p=0 fiber is audited separately but has Lebesgue measure zero unless an extra origin atom is declared
tasks: verify the frozen H=fC identity, weighted-space symmetry, unitary conjugation, and exact expanded flat operator
Fourier-decompose the candidate and derive the weighted deficiency equation
reduce the zero-energy fiber equation to the modified-Bessel equation for p nonzero and p=0
separately establish the Q-to-minus-infinity and Q-to-plus-infinity weighted integrability ledgers
apply the scoped Weyl and von Neumann guards to record one limit-circle and one limit-point endpoint per fiber
derive oscillatory Wronskian boundary coordinates for p nonzero and affine boundary coordinates for p=0
show that a fiber U(1) phase or real projective condition is extension data and is not canonically selected
record the conditional measurable-theta(p) direct-integral recipe, leave its global measurable domain/resolvent construction open, and record that p=0 is null in the Lebesgue base
independently check the Bessel differential equation and I/K Wronskian at fixed p and x samples without solving a deficiency ODE
leave the raw-C rigging map, C-to-H equivalence, endpoint transform, BFV, quantum-gravity, physics and TOE outputs null
